image.subject: a stout middle-aged clerk in a dark suit and high white collar, neat side-parted hair, sallow cautious face, sitting alone at a candlelit table in a corner of a Marseille tavern, glaring across the room at a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt dancing at a wedding feast, 1815

storyboard.claim: Danglars resents Dantes for being favored, and feels the captaincy should be his by seniority.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Danglars alone in a corner, envious glare at the dancing sailor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the feast scene; Danglars introduced as the outsider watcher.
storyboard.addedInformation: Motive is resentment at being passed over, not personal hatred.

image.subject: a stout clerk in a dark suit and high white collar leaning close across a wine table to a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket, both faces low and conspiratorial, candlelit Marseille tavern, 1815

storyboard.claim: Danglars drinks with Fernand and begins the scheme against Dantes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men leaning together over wine in a dim tavern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Danglars moves from watching to acting, pulling Fernand in.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fernand is the jealous rival who will carry out the plot.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket staring hard across a crowded wedding-feast room, his jaw tight, glaring at a lean dark-haired young sailor and a dark-haired young Catalan woman in a simple pale 1815 dress with a shawl dancing together

storyboard.claim: Fernand is jealous of Dantes and Mercedes at the feast.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand in the foreground, glaring at the couple dancing in the background.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows Danglars' plan; Fernand's jealousy is the fuel.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Fernand's jealousy is visible to everyone at the feast.

image.subject: close view of a stout clerk's left hand in a dark sleeve writing slowly on a sheet of paper by candlelight, the letters slanting, ink pot and quill on a tavern table, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Danglars writes the denunciation with his left hand to disguise his handwriting.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A left hand writing carefully on paper under candlelight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Danglars now moves from scheming to the act of writing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The disguised handwriting shows deliberate, calculated deceit.

image.subject: a sheet of paper crumpled into a ball and tossed carelessly into a dark corner of a tavern floor beside a wine bottle, candlelight, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Danglars crumples the accusation and tosses it aside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Crumpled paper lying in a dark corner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The note exists; now it is discarded.
storyboard.addedInformation: The careless toss shows he sees it as disposable.

image.subject: a stout clerk in a dark suit looking away with a bland face while passing a folded letter across a tavern table to a jealous young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Danglars hands the weapon to Fernand, calling it a joke, and looks away.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Danglars looking away as the folded note passes to Fernand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The note is in play; the handover is the trigger.
storyboard.addedInformation: Danglars manufactures the weapon while keeping deniability.

storyboard.claim: Narrator frames the next point for the listener.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; pure transition.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivot from the scene to the lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: None; banter.

storyboard.claim: Evil does not always come with a drawn sword.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; the quotation carries the idea.
storyboard.onScreenText: Evil doesn't always arrive with a drawn sword.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads from the lesson to the thesis about paper.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the contrast between violence and paperwork.

image.subject: a stack of official papers and a quill on a clerk's ledger desk in a dim 1815 counting-house, one sheet half-signed, a candle guttering beside them

storyboard.claim: Destruction happens on paper, in administrative greed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Official paperwork on a ledger desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quotation pivots to paperwork as the weapon.
storyboard.addedInformation: Administrative paper is the mechanism of harm.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket bending down to pick up a crumpled paper from a tavern floor, his face set and intent, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Fernand picks up the discarded note and will send it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand stooping to retrieve the crumpled paper.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Danglars tosses it; now Fernand takes it up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fernand becomes the courier of the accusation.

storyboard.claim: Bureaucratic detachment flows into the official who processes the paper.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; abstract transfer of responsibility.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the paper moves from Danglars to the court.
storyboard.addedInformation: Pure explanatory bridge to the magistrate.

image.subject: a sharp-faced middle-aged royal prosecutor in a black judicial coat with a white cravat, grey-streaked dark hair swept back, cold precise expression, seated behind a desk in a Marseille courthouse office, 1815 Restoration France

storyboard.claim: Villefort is the crown's prosecutor, the law's moral authority.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Villefort seated at his desk in the courthouse.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The paper reaches the magistrate's office.
storyboard.addedInformation: Villefort is introduced as the institutional authority.

image.subject: a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat with a white cravat facing a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt across a desk, the prosecutor's face softened, candlelit 1815 courthouse office

storyboard.claim: Villefort and Dantes share a moment of understanding; Villefort likes him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Prosecutor and sailor face to face across a desk, the prosecutor softened.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The magistrate meets the accused.
storyboard.addedInformation: The warmth makes the later betrayal sharper.

image.subject: a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt handing a folded letter across a desk to a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat, release papers and an inkstand on the desk, 1815 courthouse

storyboard.claim: Villefort is about to sign Dantes's release, until Dantes hands over the letter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The letter passing across the desk as release papers wait.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Warmth turns to the fatal handover.
storyboard.addedInformation: The letter from Elba is the fatal evidence.

image.subject: close-up of a folded sealed letter on a wooden desk, a candle beside it, the address side turned up, 1815 Restoration France

storyboard.claim: The letter is addressed to a Paris street, linking Dantes to the Bonapartist committee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sealed letter on a desk with a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The letter is handed over; now the address is the trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: The address names the Paris recipient that makes the letter damning.

image.subject: a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat staring down at an open letter on his desk, his hand frozen mid-motion, cold candlelight, 1815 courthouse office

storyboard.claim: Villefort reads the address and knows Dantes is innocent but realises the danger.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Villefort frozen over the open letter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The address is read; the choice begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: His frozen stillness shows the internal conflict.

image.subject: a brass balance scale on a courthouse desk, one pan holding a sealed letter and the other a gold coin, a candle beside it, 1815 Restoration office

storyboard.claim: Villefort weighs his career against the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Balance scales with letter and coin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Recognition gives way to the calculation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance motif makes the trade-off literal.

image.subject: a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat kneeling at a stone fireplace, feeding a folded letter into the flames, the paper curling to ash, 1815 office

storyboard.claim: Villefort burns the letter to protect his career.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The letter curling in the fireplace.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The calculation ends in the act.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire destroys the only evidence of Dantes's innocence.

image.subject: a rusted iron chain hanging from a damp stone wall in a dim prison cell, a single candle on the floor, 1815 island fortress

storyboard.claim: Burning the letter burns Dantes's life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chain on a stone wall in a dim cell.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fire's cost is shown on Dantes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dantes is sent to the prison fortress.

storyboard.claim: Who is the true architect of the tragedy?
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; the question is the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the plot to the moral debate.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the three culprits for comparison.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket with a tight jaw and clenched fists at a wedding-feast table, candle glow on his face, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: The speaker thinks Fernand is the most hateful, visceral in his betrayal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand at the table with clenched fists.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The debate opens with Fernand.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fernand's visible rage makes the case for him.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket smiling warmly while raising a wine glass to a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt at a candlelit betrothal feast, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Fernand smiled at Dantes's feast knowing he would send him to death.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand and Dantes raising glasses, Fernand smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Deepens Fernand's betrayal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The false friendship at the feast.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket leaning close to a dark-haired young Catalan woman in a simple pale 1815 dress with a shawl, she weeping by a window in soft candlelight

storyboard.claim: Fernand comforts Mercedes and manipulates her grief until she marries him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand leaning over a weeping Mercedes by a window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the feast to the years after.
storyboard.addedInformation: The years of manipulation show the cruelty.

image.subject: a simple gold ring lying on a folded pale shawl on a dark wooden table, candlelight, 1815 Catalan household

storyboard.claim: Fernand stole Dantes's bride and his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ring on a folded shawl.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stolen bride is made concrete.
storyboard.addedInformation: The ring stands for the stolen marriage.

storyboard.claim: Banter about who is worse.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; dialogue.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the debate toward Villefort.
storyboard.addedInformation: None; banter.

storyboard.claim: Villefort is infinitely worse than Fernand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; the verdict lands in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the debate.
storyboard.addedInformation: The verdict.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket standing on a Marseille quay at dusk, fists clenched, fishing boats and nets behind him

storyboard.claim: Fernand acted from primal, uneducated passion with no institutional power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand on the quay, fists clenched.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The argument shifts to the difference in roles.
storyboard.addedInformation: A fisherman with no power, not an official.

image.subject: a young Catalan fisherman in a faded blue jacket backed against a rough stone wall in a dark Marseille alley, arms raised, face strained, lantern light, 1815

storyboard.claim: Fernand is an animal backed into a corner by love and jealousy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand backed against a wall in the alley.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the passion argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cornered desperation of the crime of passion.

image.subject: a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat standing in a stone courthouse hall beneath a brass scales of justice, 1815 Restoration France

storyboard.claim: Villefort was the sworn protector of the law.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Villefort in the courthouse hall beneath the scales.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The argument shifts to Villefort's role.
storyboard.addedInformation: His duty makes his betrayal worse.

storyboard.claim: Society gave the magistrate a sacred duty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None; the three duties are the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Lists the duties Villefort had.
storyboard.addedInformation: The three duties make the betrayal clear.

image.subject: a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt, barely nineteen, standing pale before a prosecutor's desk in a courthouse office, 1815 Marseille

storyboard.claim: Villefort looked at a 19-year-old and calculated the cost of his life.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Young Dantes before the desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the calculation.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dantes's youth is the stake in the calculation.

left.label: THE KID'S LIFE
left.subject: a lean dark-haired young sailor in plain sailor's linen shirt sitting in a dim stone cell, head bowed, a single candle

right.label: THE PROMOTION
right.subject: a sharp-faced prosecutor in a black judicial coat at a polished desk, a promotion letter under his hand, candlelight

storyboard.claim: Villefort traded Dantes's life for his career.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dantes in a cell versus Villefort at a desk with a promotion letter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the calculation into a visual trade.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trade is the corruption of justice.

image.subject: a heavy iron stamp pressed into red wax on a stack of legal papers in a dim Restoration courthouse, a candle beside it

storyboard.claim: Villefort weaponized the state apparatus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A stamp pressed into red wax on legal papers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The trade becomes the abuse of the state.
storyboard.addedInformation: The seal shows official power used for harm.

image.subject: a cracked stone wall of an old Marseille house with damp stains spreading through it, a single candle glowing inside a window, 1815

storyboard.claim: Villefort's crime rots the foundation of society, while Fernand's destroys a family.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cracked wall with spreading damp.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the two crimes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The crack stands for the damaged foundation.

image.subject: a stout clerk in a dark suit walking away down a sunlit Paris boulevard, not looking back, 1820s

storyboard.claim: The three men walk away and move on while Dantes waits in a cell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A man in a dark suit walking away down a sunlit street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequences are left behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: The men feel no guilt.

image.subject: a handsome dark-haired man in his thirties in a dark military coat with epaulettes, a Parisian general standing in a gilded salon, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Fernand becomes a military general built on the momentum of his lie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fernand as general in a gilded salon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fortunes are built.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fernand's rise in the 1830s.

image.subject: a stout middle-aged clerk in a dark suit and high white collar in a gilded Paris bank office with ledgers and gold coins on the desk, 1830s

storyboard.claim: Danglars becomes a wealthy baron and banker in Paris.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Danglars in a gilded bank office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the fortunes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Danglars rises to the bond market.

image.subject: a gaunt lean young man with long hair and a beard in a stone cell, tally marks scratched into the wall, a grey light from a high window, 1820s island fortress

storyboard.claim: The years compound on Dantes in the stone box.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Dantes in the cell with tally marks on the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The men move on; Dantes stays.
storyboard.addedInformation: The tally marks count the years.

image.subject: a sand hourglass on a stone prison ledge beside a single candle, dim cell light, 1820s island fortress

storyboard.claim: In the dark, time is a long-term investment, a waiting period.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass on a stone ledge.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Time becomes the metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass is the waiting.

image.subject: a canvas burial sack being hauled over the side of a dark smuggler's boat at night on the Mediterranean, lanterns and moonlight on the water, 1820s

storyboard.claim: Dantes escapes in Faria's burial sack and is picked up by smugglers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sack hauled onto a smuggler's boat at night.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The vault finally opens.
storyboard.addedInformation: The escape is through the dead man's sack.
